rv.q: In every way, a prodigious evening.
There is enormous pleasure to be had in the smallest details of Tennant’s performance.
Tennant gives us a memorable portrayal of the desolation of hedonism.
The production is uneven, not to mention borderline tacky at times (silly dancing, good karaoke). But it is also funny, acerbic, biting.
Marber’s revival may not cut as deeply as some might wish, but it is certainly sharp.
I just found it easier to shut my conscience off and laugh.
This is a play trying to have it both ways, exposing decadence while simultaneously charging big money for that very sort of titillation.
Despite some moments of laughter, this is probably Juan to miss.
And while it seeks to charm and outrage in equal measure, it ends up being charmless and creepy.
Both script and performance walk the tightrope of genuine comedy and near disgust with aplomb.
Tennant's thrill-seeking has its limits, and it's hard to believe him throwing himself headlong into an offstage street brawl just for the hell of it.
But the tone of this slapdash play keeps shifting.
But no amount of swagger can forestall one’s sense of the play as a theatrical exercise...
A red-light from me, then, for this flaccid affair although, for some, the temptation to ogle Tennant in the flesh will prove too great to resist.
Marber's revival may not cut as deeply as some might wish, but it is certainly sharp.
Tennant is brimful of charisma but lacks the charm of a consummate seducer.
Tennant's V-sign at the curtain call is superfluous since the entire production is an affront to the audience.

cn.t: Tennant charms in Marber's bracing, brutal update of Molière, though critics split on whether the modernized libertine tale truly resonates. Most praise the lead performances and dark comedy, but some find it shallow and misogynistic.
